(Paris, France) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (2021–2025) | years1 = 2020–2021 | team1 = [[Nanterre 92]] | highlights = * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2025) * Second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] (2024) * [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player of The Year|Pac-12 Most Improved Player]] (2024) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|FRA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U20 European Championship]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2023 FIBA U20 European Championship|2023 Greece]]|[[France men's national under-20 basketball team|Team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA U16 European Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship|2019 Italy]]|[[France national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Maxime Pierre Raynaud''' (Born 7 April 2003) is a French [[college basketball]] player for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). ==College career== Raynaud graduated from [[Lycée Henri-IV]] in his native Paris. Seeking to play [[college basketball]] in the United States, Raynaud committed to the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]].{{cite news|first=Travis|last=Branham|title= 2021 French big man Maxime Raynaud commits to Stanford |url= https://247sports.com/article/maxime-raynaud-basketball-stanford-commitment-165390714/ | date = 14 May 2021| website= 247sports.com | publisher = [[247Sports.com]]|access-date=3 April 2025}} He established himself as a part of the Cardinal rotation under coach [[Jerod Haase]] in his first two seasons. As a junior in the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]], Raynaud saw an increase in his productivity, averaging 15.5 points and 9.6 rebounds per game. He was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and the Most Improved Player in the conference. With the firing of Haase at the close of the season, Raynaud entered the transfer portal and considered leaving Stanford, but ultimately chose to remain and play for new coach [[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]] in Stanford's inaugural season in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].{{cite news|first=Grant|last=Grubbs|title= Stanford forward Maxime Raynaud withdraws from NCAA Transfer Portal |url= https://www.on3.com/transfer-portal/news/stanford-forward-maxime-raynaud-withdraws-from-ncaa-transfer-portal/ | date = 19 April 2024| website= on3.com | publisher = [[On3.com]]|access-date=3 April 2025}}{{cite news|first=Janie|last=McCauley|title= Maxime Raynaud’s return to Stanford has meant so much to him and the program |url= https://apnews.com/article/maxime-raynaud-stanford-transfer-portal-798234703e7c710558846da8c8d677df | date = 28 February 2025| website= apnews.com | publisher = [[Associated Press]]|access-date=8 March 2025}} At the close of the season, Raynaud was named the recipient of the [[Skip Prosser]] Award for top scholar-athlete in the ACC.{{cite press release|title= ND’s Miles, Stanford’s Raynaud Earn ACC Basketball Scholar-Athlete of the Year Honors |url= https://theacc.com/news/2025/3/5/mens-basketball-nds-miles-stanfords-raynaud-earn-acc-basketball-scholar-athlete-of-the-year-honors.aspx | date = 5 March 2025| website= theacc.com | publisher = [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=8 March 2025}} ==French national team== Raynaud has been a member of the [[France men's national basketball team|France national team]], competing at several levels of their junior program. He was a starter on the French team who won gold at the [[2023 FIBA U20 European Championship]], leading the team in scoring (26) in their championship win over Israel.{{cite news |title= Raynaud, Kamardine and Yaacov put on a show, as France outlast Israel |url= https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/europe-u20-2023-news-raynaud-kamardine-and-yaacov-put-on-a-show-as-france-outlast-israel | date = 26 July 2023| publisher = [[FIBA]]|access-date=3 April 2025}} ==See also== *[[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://gostanford.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/player/maxime-raynaud Stanford Cardinal bio] *[https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/271297-maxime-raynaud FIBA profile] *[https://www.lnb.fr/espoirs-elite/joueur/?id=6489 LNB Élite profile] {{DEFAULTSORT:Raynaud, Maxime}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Paris]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:French expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:French men's basketball players]] [[Category:Lycée Henri-IV alumni]] [[Category:Nanterre 92 players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Stanford Cardinal men's basketball players]]
